# Research: Parameter Exploration & Sharing

**Feature**: `003-parameter-exploration` | **Date**: 2026-08-10

Six decisions this plan needed to resolve before Phase 1 design, each
grounded in the actual shipped code (`src/concepts/rag/`), not assumed
from the spec alone.

## Decision: Chunk-size sweep range and point count (FR-001, FR-002)

**Decision**: 9 points, generated by `generateSweepChunkSizes()`:
linearly interpolate 9 values across `[20, 120]` (the existing
chunk-size slider's own `min`/`max` in `ChunkingStep.tsx`), then round
each to the nearest multiple of 5 (the slider's own `step`), giving:

```
[20, 35, 45, 60, 70, 85, 95, 110, 120]
```

**Rationale**: `/speckit.clarify` (2026-08-10) fixed the range to the
existing slider's bounds and the point count to 8-10, specifically to
avoid a second, competing range control. Rounding to the slider's own
step (5) keeps every sweep point a value the learner could also reach
by dragging the slider themselves -- the sweep is a "run all the
slider's meaningful positions at once" feature, not a separate
parameter space.

**Alternatives considered**: An unrounded even split (20, 32.5, 45, ...)
was rejected -- fractional chunk sizes don't correspond to any reachable
slider position, which would make a sweep point's "jump to this
configuration" (FR-002) land somewhere the learner couldn't have
navigated to by hand, undermining the curve's role as a navigable
summary rather than a separate simulation.

## Decision: Per-point overlap clamping (Edge Cases)

**Decision**: Each sweep point clamps overlap independently:
`clampedOverlap = Math.min(overlap, chunkSizeAtPoint - 5)`, mirroring
`ChunkingStep.tsx`'s existing slider-max formula
(`Math.min(40, chunkSize - 5)`). The learner's own overlap slider value
is never mutated by a sweep -- only the value fed into that one point's
chunking call.

**Rationale**: Directly resolves the Edge Case named in spec.md: a
sweep range can include chunk sizes where the current overlap setting
would be structurally invalid (overlap >= chunk size) at some points but
not others. Clamping per-point, not just at the sweep's starting value,
is the only way to keep every point's chunking call valid.

## Decision: Sweep metric (top-1 similarity score)

**Decision**: `ranked[0]?.score ?? 0` -- the cosine similarity of the
single highest-ranked chunk, computed before Top-K slicing or
similarity-threshold filtering.

**Rationale**: `/speckit.clarify` fixed the metric to top-1 similarity
score only, matching spec.md's own example phrasing. Measuring it
*before* threshold/Top-K filtering (rather than the current filtered
`topResults`) isolates the sweep's teaching point -- "does this chunk
size dilute or sharpen the best possible match" -- from the two other,
already-teachable controls (FR-013's threshold, existing Top-K), which
would otherwise conflate three variables in one curve.

## Decision: Concurrent-sweep cancellation

**Decision**: A monotonically increasing `sweepToken` (component state,
incremented on every "Start sweep" click). Each in-flight Real Mode
per-point fetch closure captures the token it was started with and
discards its result if `token !== currentSweepTokenRef.current` by the
time it resolves -- the same `cancelled` closure-flag pattern
`RetrievalStep.tsx` already uses for its corpus/query embed effects,
extended to a counter since a sweep has many sequential calls instead of
one.

**Rationale**: `/speckit.clarify` resolved the spec's own open
either/or (cancel vs. queue) in favor of cancel-and-replace. Reusing the
token/closure pattern already proven in `RetrievalStep.tsx` avoids
introducing a second cancellation idiom into the same file.

## Decision: Real Mode sweep call cost

**Decision**: `N + 1` real API calls per sweep run, where `N` is the
point count (9): one `corpus-embed` call per point (each point re-chunks
the document at a different size, so each has a genuinely different
corpus to embed) plus a single shared `query-embed` call (the query text
itself doesn't change across a chunk-size sweep, so it's fetched once
and reused for all 9 points' scoring).

**Rationale**: Mirrors `callEstimate.ts`'s existing formula style
(`hydeCallCount`, `fusionCallCount`) and its cache-what's-reusable
principle (corpus embedding is already cached per document/chunk-settings
elsewhere in the codebase). `N + 1` is always greater than one call, so
FR-003's cost-confirmation gate is unconditionally triggered for every
Real Mode sweep -- consistent with spec.md's Acceptance Scenario 4.

## Decision: Sweep curve keyboard operability (Constitution VII)

**Decision**: `SweepCurve.tsx` renders its axis/line as a decorative,
`aria-hidden` SVG background, with each data point rendered as a real
HTML `<button>` absolutely positioned on top of it (a `position:
relative` wrapper, buttons positioned via inline `style={{ left, top }}`
computed from the same screen-space math `StarChart.tsx` uses), not as
an SVG shape with a manually-added `tabIndex`.

**Rationale**: `/speckit.clarify` required every point to be individually
focusable and Enter/Space-activatable. Milestone 1's own history
(`roadmap.md`'s 2026-08-05 update) found real, previously-invisible
accessibility defects in this project's SVG chart interactions -- a
native `<button>` gets correct focus order, activation semantics, and
accessible naming for free from the browser, rather than re-deriving
that behavior on an SVG primitive that wasn't designed to carry it.

## Decision: Where sweep/permalink/preset state and controls live

**Decision**: All three new controls (`SweepPanel` inside
`RetrievalStep.tsx`, `PermalinkButton`, `FailurePresetPicker`) read and
write state already owned by `PipelineWalkthrough.tsx` -- `docId`,
`chunkSize`, `overlap`, `chunkingStrategy`, `query`,
`similarityThreshold` are all local `useState` there already, and
`realMode`/`generationParams`/`topK` are already threaded down to it as
props from `RagConcept.tsx`. No new state is lifted to `RagConcept.tsx`.

**Rationale**: FR-005's permalink enumeration and US3's preset
configuration both need exactly the set of parameters
`PipelineWalkthrough.tsx` already owns end-to-end. Lifting them one
level higher to `RagConcept.tsx` (which doesn't currently hold any of
them) would be a larger, unjustified blast radius for no behavioral
gain -- Compare Variants already keeps its own independent copy of
document/query state per the 002-real-mode "independent state" decision,
and neither the sweep nor the permalink nor the presets are spec'd to
apply there.

## Decision: Permalink transport (query string, not an opaque blob)

**Decision**: Plain `URLSearchParams` query keys (`mode`, `doc`, `cs`,
`ov`, `strat`, `th`, `k`, `q`, and, Real-Mode-only, `temp`, `fn`, `hc`),
read via Next.js's `useSearchParams()` and written via
`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` -- no base64/compression encoding, no
new dependency.

**Rationale**: A human-inspectable query string makes SC-002 ("every
permalink, when inspected, contains zero API keys or credentials")
verifiable *by a learner directly*, not just by the automated check --
an opaque encoded blob would require decoding to audit, which cuts
against the same transparency principle SC-002 exists to protect.

**Next.js constraint discovered**: `useSearchParams()` is a Client
Component hook; because `src/app/concepts/[conceptId]/page.tsx` is
statically generated (`generateStaticParams`), Next's own docs
(`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/use-search-params.md`)
require the calling component to sit under a `<Suspense>` boundary or
the production build fails outright ("Missing Suspense boundary with
useSearchParams"). This plan therefore wraps `<Component />` in
`page.tsx` with `<Suspense>` -- one generic edit applying uniformly to
every concept module (this file has no RAG-specific or
`concept.id`-keyed logic before or after the change), so it doesn't trip
`check:extensibility`'s conditional-scan or Principle I.

## Decision: Failure-preset verification mechanism (SC-004)

**Decision**: `scripts/checks/failure-presets.ts`, a pure-function
check in the same style as `determinism.ts` -- no browser, no
Playwright. For each shipped `FailurePreset`, it runs the actual
`chunkText`/`chunkTextBySentence`, `embed`, and `cosineSimilarity`
functions against the preset's exact configuration and asserts a
structural predicate:

- **threshold-too-strict**: the ranked-and-filtered result set is empty
  (`ranked.filter(r => r.score >= threshold).length === 0`).
- **chunk-too-large** / **chunk-too-small**: a specific fact substring
  (e.g. a full sentence naming two related numbers) is present in the
  source document but is **not** contained whole within any single
  produced chunk at the preset's chunk size -- i.e. the fact is split
  across a chunk boundary.

**Rationale**: Directly answers the Edge Case named in spec.md ("what
happens if a failure preset stops reproducing its failure after an
unrelated engine change") -- because this check imports and calls the
*live* pipeline functions rather than storing expected numbers, a
chunking-algorithm change that quietly stops producing the labeled
failure fails this check immediately, the same guarantee
`determinism.ts` already provides for SC-006.
